detail.readme: # GIMP MCP [![License: GPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPLv3-blue.svg)](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0) [![Works with Claude Desktop](https://img.shields.io/badge/Works%20with-Claude%20Desktop-7B2CBF.svg)](https://claude.ai/desktop) [![GIMP 3.2](https://img.shields.io/badge/GIMP-3.2-orange.svg)](https://gimp.org) [![MCP Compatible](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-Compatible-green.svg)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) [![CodeRabbit](https://img.shields.io/badge/CodeRabbit-AI%20Review-171717?logo=coderabbit)](https://coderabbit.ai) ## Demo ![GIMP MCP in action — AI agent driving GIMP through natural language](docs/mcpInAction.gif) Full demo (with audio): https://github.com/gimp-mcp/gimp-mcp/raw/main/docs/demo.mp4 *AI agent using GIMP MCP to remove a background, edit a character's expression, and verify results — all through natural language via Claude* --- ## Overview GIMP MCP bridges GIMP's professional image editing capabilities with AI assistants through the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). It lets you edit images by describing what you want — and gives the AI a live visual feedback channel to verify each change before moving on. **What makes it different from other GIMP integrations:** - The AI can *see* the image at any point in the workflow without saving to disk (`get_state_snapshot`) - Supports fully autonomous multi-step pipelines: open → edit → verify → refine → export - 79 dedicated tool commands covering every major GIMP operation - Fully compatible with GIMP 3.2.x (all breaking API changes resolved) ## Key Features | | | |---|---| | 👁️ **Live Visual Feedback** | `get_state_snapshot` returns a PNG preview mid-workflow so the AI verifies each step | | 🎨 **79 GIMP Tools** | Adjustments, transforms, selections, layers, drawing, text, filters — all via MCP | | 🔧 **GIMP 3.2 Compatible** | All GIMP 3.2 API breaks fixed and tested (59/59 passing) | | 🔁 **Iterative Workflows** | AI loops until a goal is met — e.g. keeps removing BG until no pixels remain | | 🖼️ **Region Snapshots** | Zoom into any area for detail verification (face, mouth, corner, etc.) | | 🔌 **Universal MCP** | Works with Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, PydanticAI, and more | ## What Can It Do? ### Background Removal with Iterative Verification The AI removes the background, takes a snapshot to inspect the result, detects remaining pixels, and loops until the image is clean: ``` "Remove the background from this image and keep looping until only the character remains" ``` ### Expression Editing ``` "Make the character smile — paint a smile arc with teeth over her mouth" ``` ### Complex Multi-Step Pipelines ``` "Open navi_portrait.png, remove the background, verify it's clean, then make her smile and export the final result as a PNG" ``` ### Color & Tone Work ``` "Boost the contrast, shift the hue 15 degrees warmer, then show me a before/after zoom of the face" ``` ### Text & Compositing ``` "Add a bold title at the top in white with a subtle drop shadow, then export for web" ``` --- ## Prerequisites - **GIMP 3.2+** — tested on GIMP 3.2.2 (Windows, macOS, Linux) - **uv** — Python package manager ([install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/)); `uvx` downloads the MCP server and a suitable Python (3.11+) on first use - **MCP-compatible AI client** — Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, PydanticAI, etc. --- ## Quick Start The MCP server and the GIMP plugin ship together as the [`gimp-mcp-plugin`](https://pypi.org/project/gimp-mcp-plugin/) package on PyPI. No clone needed. ### 1. Install the GIMP Plugin Launch GIMP once (so its config folder exists), close it, then run: ```bash uvx gimp-mcp-plugin@latest install-plugin ``` This copies the plugin into the newest GIMP 3.x config folder it finds (Linux standard, Snap and Flatpak locations, macOS, Windows) and makes it executable. Restart GIMP afterward. - `--dry-run` shows where it would install without writing anything. - `--gimp-dir DIR` installs into a specific GIMP config folder, e.g. `--gimp-dir ~/.config/GIMP/3.2`. If you have more than one GIMP 3 installation (e.g. a system GIMP and a Flatpak), the newest folder found may not be the one your GIMP uses. Check the folder shown in GIMP's **Edit → Preferences → Folders → Plug-ins** and pass the folder that contains `plug-ins` with `--gimp-dir`. > **Which folder does GIMP use?** GIMP names its per-user folder after its **major.minor** > version (`3.0`, `3.2`, `3.4`, …) and creates a fresh one on each minor upgrade, so the > plug-ins folder *moves* when you upgrade GIMP. Re-run `install-plugin` after upgrading. > To check the active path, open **Edit → Preferences → Folders → Plug-ins** in GIMP. ### 2. Start the MCP Server in GIMP 1. Open any image in GIMP 2. Go to **Tools > MCP > Start MCP Server** 3. Server starts on `localhost:9877` #### Start automatically when GIMP launches To skip step 2 on every launch, open **Tools > MCP > MCP Server Settings...**, tick **Start MCP server when GIMP launches**, and restart GIMP. Autostart is off by default. The same dialog sets the **port** (default `9877`). If you change it, set `GIMP_MCP_PORT` in your MCP client config so the MCP server connects to the same port: ```json "gimp": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["gimp-mcp-plugin@latest"], "env": { "GIMP_MCP_PORT": "9988" } } ``` Settings are saved to `gimp-mcp.json` in GIMP's per-user config folder (e.g. `~/.config/GIMP/3.2/gimp-mcp.json`). Port changes apply the next time the server starts. #### Timeout for long commands The MCP server waits up to 300 seconds for GIMP to finish each command. For heavier work (large or 16-bit images, slow filters), set `GIMP_MCP_TIMEOUT` (in seconds) in your MCP client config, the same way as `GIMP_MCP_PORT` above, e.g. `"GIMP_MCP_TIMEOUT": "900"`. `check_server` reports the timeout in effect. When a command times out, GIMP may still be running it, so check the image before retrying. Your MCP client may have its own tool timeout (in Claude Code, `MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT`, in milliseconds); raise it too if it's shorter. ### 3. Configure Your MCP Client `gimp-mcp-plugin@latest` makes `uvx` check PyPI for a new release each time your client starts the server. #### Claude Desktop `~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (Linux/macOS) or `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` (Windows): ```json { "mcpServers": { "gimp": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["gimp-mcp-plugin@latest"] } } } ``` #### Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add gimp-mcp -- uvx gimp-mcp-plugin@latest ``` #### Gemini CLI `~/.config/gemini/.gemini_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "gimp": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["gimp-mcp-plugin@latest"] } } } ``` #### PydanticAI ```python from pydantic_ai import Agent from pydantic_ai.mcp import MCPServerStdio server = MCPServerStdio('uvx', args=['gimp-mcp-plugin@latest']) agent = Agent('openai:gpt-4o', mcp_servers=[server]) ``` #### Cancelling long commands GIMP runs one command at a time, in the order they're sent. While it works, the MCP server stays responsive, so your client can cancel a call. The cancel returns at once: a command that's still waiting its turn never runs, but one GIMP has already started is finished in the background. Check the image before retrying a cancelled edit, or it may be applied twice. ### Updating The plugin and the MCP server must be the same version. `check_server` and `get_gimp_info` report a mismatch and print the command that fixes it. To update both: 1. Restart your MCP client. With `@latest`, it picks up the newest server. 2. Run `uvx gimp-mcp-plugin@latest install-plugin` and restart GIMP. ### Running from a Git Checkout (contributors) To work on the code, run the server and install the plugin from a clone instead: ```bash git clone https://github.com/gimp-mcp/gimp-mcp.git cd gimp-mcp uv sync uv run gimp_mcp_server.py install-plugin # installs this checkout's plugin ``` Then point your MCP client at the checkout, e.g. for Claude Desktop: ```json "gimp": { "command": "uv", "args": ["run", "--directory", "/full/path/to/gimp-mcp", "gimp_mcp_server.py"] } ``` Claude Code picks up the repo's `.mcp.json` automatically when started in the checkout. After `git pull`, re-run `install-plugin` if the plugin changed. --- ## Available MCP Tools ### 👁️ Visual Feedback #### `get_state_snapshot(image_index, max_size, region, label)` Returns a live PNG of the current image state — the AI's primary feedback mechanism. Call this between any edits to verify the result without saving to disk. ```python # Full image snapshot snapshot = get_state_snapshot(max_size=512) # Zoom into a face region for detail inspection snapshot = get_state_snapshot( region={"x": 140, "y": 80, "width": 240, "height": 300}, max_size=512, label="face-check" ) ``` This enables iterative agentic workflows: **edit → snapshot → assess → refine → repeat**. #### `get_image_bitmap(image_index, max_width, max_height, region)` Lower-level bitmap fetch with region extraction and scaling. Returns base64-encoded PNG. ### 🎨 Adjustments | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `adjust_brightness_contrast` | Brightness and contrast | | `adjust_curves` | Curves by channel (RGB/R/G/B/A) | | `adjust_hue_saturation` | Hue, saturation, lightness | | `adjust_color_balance` | Shadows/midtones/highlights color balance | | `auto_levels` | Auto-stretch levels | | `desaturate` | Convert to grayscale (keep RGB mode) | | `invert_colors` | Invert all channels | | `convert_color_mode` | Convert between RGB, grayscale, and indexed modes | | `sharpen` | Unsharp mask sharpening | | `blur` | Gaussian blur | | `denoise` | Noise reduction | ### 🔄 Transforms | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `scale_image` | Scale to exact dimensions | | `scale_to_fit` | Scale within bounding box (aspect-safe) | | `crop_to_rect` | Crop to rectangle | | `crop_to_selection` | Crop canvas to the current selection bounds | | `rotate_image` | Rotate 90/180/270 or arbitrary angle | | `flip_image` | Flip horizontal or vertical | | `resize_canvas` | Resize canvas without scaling content | | `warp_region` | Warp / liquify a region by pushing pixels in a direction | ### ✂️ Selections | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `select_rectangle` | Rectangular marquee | | `select_ellipse` | Elliptical marquee | | `select_by_color` | Select by color (global) | | `select_all` / `select_none` | Select all / deselect | | `invert_selection` | Invert selection | | `modify_selection` | Grow, shrink, feather, or border | ### 🗂️ Layers | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `create_layer` | New empty layer | | `duplicate_layer` | Duplicate active layer | | `delete_layer` | Delete named layer | | `rename_layer` | Rename layer | | `set_layer_properties` | Opacity, blend mode, visibility | | `reorder_layer` | Move layer in stack | | `merge_visible_layers` | Flatten visible to one layer | | `flatten_image` | Flatten all layers | | `list_layers` | List all layers with properties | ### 🖌️ Drawing & Fill | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `fill_layer` | Fill entire layer with color | | `fill_selection` | Fill selection (foreground/background/transparent) | | `fill_rectangle` | Fill a rectangle region | `gradient_fill` | Apply linear or radial gradient | | `set_colors` | Set foreground/background colors | ### 🔤 Text | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `add_text` | Add a text layer | | `edit_text` | Edit existing text layer | | `list_fonts` | List available fonts | ### ✨ Filters & Effects | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `apply_gaussian_blur` | Gaussian blur filter | | `apply_pixelate` | Pixelate/mosaic effect | | `apply_emboss` | Emboss effect | | `apply_vignette` | Vignette darkening | | `apply_noise` | Add noise/grain | | `apply_drop_shadow` | Drop shadow effect | ### 📁 File Operations | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `open_image` | Open image file | | `open_image_as_layer` | Import an image file as a new layer in an open image | | `export_image` | Export to PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, BMP | | `save_xcf` | Save as GIMP XCF (preserves layers and metadata) | | `new_canvas` | Create blank canvas | | `close_image` | Close image | | `list_images` | List open images | | `set_active_image` | Bring a specific open image to the front | ### 📦 Batch & Multi-Format Export | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `batch_export` | Export all open images (or one) to a directory | | `batch_resize` | Resize all open images to a common size | | `export_web_optimized` | Export as JPEG and PNG, keeping the smaller | | `export_icon_sizes` | Export a full Android or iOS icon set | | `export_social_media_kit` | Export resized versions for social media platforms | | `export_sprite_sheet` | Combine frames into a sprite sheet PNG | ### ↩️ History | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `undo` | Not supported on GIMP 3.x: returns an error (use Ctrl+Z in GIMP) | | `redo` | Not supported on GIMP 3.x: returns an error (use Ctrl+Y in GIMP) | ### 🔍 Info & Context | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `get_image_metadata` | Image size, mode, layers, filename | | `get_gimp_info` | GIMP version, platform, capabilities | | `get_context_state` | Current colors, brush, opacity, mode | | `get_pixel_color` | Color value at a specific pixel | | `get_histogram` | Histogram data for a channel | | `get_selection_bounds` | Current selection bounds | ### 🔌 Connection & Raw API | Tool | Description | |---|---| | `check_server` | Check the GIMP plugin socket is reachable and that the plugin version matches the server | | `restart_server` | Drop and re-establish the connection to the plugin | | `call_api` | Run arbitrary Python-Fu code inside GIMP (escape hatch for anything not covered above) | --- ## AI Agent Feedback Loop The `get_state_snapshot` tool enables a pattern where the AI loops until a goal is visually confirmed: ```text ┌─────────────┐ │ Apply edit │ └──────┬──────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ get_state_ │ ← AI sees live PNG, no disk save needed │ snapshot() │ └──────┬──────────┘ │ ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ │ Goal achieved? │─ No─▶ Adjust & retry │ └──────┬──────────┘ └──────────────────┘ │ Yes ▼ ┌─────────────┐ │ Export │ └─────────────┘ ``` ### Example: Iterative Background Removal See [`bg_remove_iterative.py`](bg_remove_iterative.py) for a complete example. The AI: 1. Removes the background using edge-seeded contiguous select 2. Takes a snapshot to check the result 3. Scans for remaining background-colored pixels 4. Runs targeted removal passes with progressively finer grids (25px → 1px) 5. Runs a final despeckle pass for isolated pixels 6. Loops until no background pixels remain --- ## Example Scripts | Script | Description | |---|---| | [`run_tests.py`](run_tests.py) | 59-test suite — run against your GIMP to verify all tools work | | [`bg_remove_iterative.py`](bg_remove_iterative.py) | Iterative BG removal with snapshot checkpoints | | [`bg_remove.py`](bg_remove.py) | Simple single-pass background removal | | [`agent_edit_demo.py`](agent_edit_demo.py) | Full pipeline: open → remove BG → edit expression → export | | [`tests/test_add_text_metadata.py`](tests/test_add_text_metadata.py) | Regression test: `add_text` returns real layer metadata | | [`tests/continuous_edit_test/continuous_edit_test.py`](tests/continuous_edit_test/continuous_edit_test.py) | End-to-end agent editing loop: BG removal, selective recolor, composite | Run the test suite to verify your setup: ```bash python run_tests.py # Expected: 59/59 PASSED ``` --- ## Technical Architecture ### Plugin ↔ Server Communication ```text AI Client (Claude, etc.) │ MCP (stdio) ▼ gimp_mcp_server.py ← MCP tool definitions │ TCP JSON :9877 ▼ gimp-mcp-plugin.py ← Runs inside GIMP process │ PyGObject ▼ GIMP 3.2 (gi.repository.Gimp) ``` - MCP server translates tool calls into JSON commands sent to the plugin over TCP - Plugin executes operations directly in the GIMP process via PyGObject - Two message formats: `{"type": "...", "params": {...}}` for named tools, `{"cmds": ["python..."]}` for arbitrary exec ### GIMP 3.2 Compatibility Notes GIMP 3.x introduced breaking API changes from GIMP 2.x. Key fixes included in this release: | Issue | Fix | |---|---| | `layer.copy(False)` → error | `layer.copy()` takes no args in GIMP 3.2 | | `Gimp.text_fontname()` removed | Use PDB `gimp-text-fontname` | | `gimp-blend` removed | Use GEGL `gegl:linear-gradient` / `gegl:radial-gradient` | | `GimpDoubleArray` TypeError in curves | Use `drawable.curves_spline()` directly | | `Gimp.fonts_get_list()` returns `Font` objects | Convert via `.get_name()` before JSON serialization | | `image.select_none()` removed | Use PDB `gimp-selection-none` | | `layer.get_pixel()` returns `Gegl.Color` | Use `.get_rgba()` to extract float components | --- ## Troubleshooting ### "Could not connect to GIMP" - GIMP must be running with an image open - Start the MCP server: **Tools > MCP > Start MCP Server**, or enable autostart in **Tools > MCP > MCP Server Settings...** - If you changed the port in GIMP, set `GIMP_MCP_PORT` to the same value in your MCP client config - Check port 9877 (or your custom port) is not blocked by firewall ### "GIMP did not reply within 300 s" - The command took longer than the MCP server waits. Raise `GIMP_MCP_TIMEOUT` (seconds) in your MCP client config; see [Timeout for long commands](#timeout-for-long-commands) - GIMP may still be running the command: check the image before retrying ### Plugin Not Visible in GIMP - Look under **Tools > MCP** (the plugin adds an `MCP` submenu, not a top-level `Tools` entry) - Confirm the plugin file is in the correct directory: `uvx gimp-mcp-plugin@latest install-plugin --dry-run` shows where it goes - **Upgraded GIMP recently?** A minor upgrade (e.g. 3.0 → 3.2) moves the per-user config folder to a new version directory; re-run `uvx gimp-mcp-plugin@latest install-plugin` (use `--dry-run` to see which folder it picks). Verify the active path via **Edit > Preferences > Folders > Plug-ins**. - On Linux/macOS: ensure the file has execute permission (`chmod +x`) - Restart GIMP after installation - Check **Filters > Script-Fu > Console** for error messages ### Tests Failing Run the test suite and check the failure list: ```bash python run_tests.py ``` Each failure includes the tool name and error — most issues on GIMP 3.2 are covered by the fixes above. --- ## Example Output *"Draw me a face and a sheep" — generated entirely through natural language via GIMP MCP* --- ## Future Enhancements - **📚 Recipe Collection**: Reusable workflow templates (portrait cleanup, product photo, etc.) - **🚀 Dynamic Discovery**: Auto-generate MCP tools from GIMP's full PDB procedure database - **🔒 Security**: Sandboxed execution for untrusted command inputs - **⚡ Performance**: Optimized bitmap transfer for large images - **🌐 Remote Access**: Network-accessible GIMP instances --- ## Contributing Contributions are welcome — bug fixes, new tools, documentation, or example scripts. Open a PR or issue on GitHub. ### Development Setup Install dev dependencies and activate the pre-commit hook so `ruff` runs on every commit: ```bash uv sync uv run pre-commit install ``` After this, `ruff` checks staged files on each `git commit` (with `--fix` applied automatically). The same check runs in CI, so the hook is just a fast local safety net. To bump the pinned hook versions later: ```bash uv run pre-commit autoupdate ``` ## License GPL-3.0-or-later.
